A plea from a personal stylist \u2b07\ufe0f...Do you know how many times I\u2019ve heard \u201cthere\u2019s the work me and then the non work me\u201d. The thought of having to separate yourself based on your environment always leaves me feeling sick. I just want to scream, \u201cyou can be both!!! You don\u2019t have to mask!!\u201dMaybe it was inceptioned by movies and pop culture. Maybe it\u2019s how we saw our mothers dressing or maybe it\u2019s the suspicion of not being taken seriously unless we dress \u201cseriously.\u201dSomewhere along the way most people started to believe that \u201cprofessional\u201d was some iteration of \u201cthe black pant suit.\u201dI\u2019m a personal stylist and wardrobe specialist whose helped so many boss woman express themselves through personal style while still commanding a room. I can tell you the strategy rarely involves a black pantsuit.At the heart of an outfit, the ONLY thing that determines \u201cprofessional\u201d is shape, quality and condition of clothing. (Nothing says unprofessional more than a pit stained, pilled or rumpled garment) There is nothing about layers, colours or patterns that take away from professional, yet it\u2019s an area I see very little experimentation in. The truth about someone taking you seriously comes from whether or not you feel confident and good in the clothing you wear. So I leave you with this: how could you add a little more interest into your work outfit this week? It can be a brooch, a scarf, a pop of colour or a simple pattern.#officeoutfits #officeoutfit #polkadotskirt #chunkysweater #bossgirls #bossgirl #whattowear #workfashion

Want to learn how to make colour work knitting, with no need to manage pesky floats? Look no further! Double knitting might be the perfect solution!Double knitting is a deceptively simple technique in which you knit two pieces of fabric back to back at the same time, alternating between working on each side with every stitch. This creates lovely thick garments which can have gorgeous colourwork designs that are neat (and inversed) on each side, making it perfect for garments like scarves where both sides are on show! I\u2019ve been offline for a bit as I had a nasty pneumonia which has taken a long time to recover from, but I\u2019ve been asked for more detail on how I double knit for ages so figured I would come back with my most requested video!In this one I am working on the Adventures of Family Fox scarf pattern which I was very kindly #gifted by @katharina.kuntz (whose Over The Garden Wall scarf pattern also features). I\u2019m making it for my husband for Christmas and currently have about 400 rows left to do- do you think I\u2019ll make it in time?? Preheat oven to 170\u00b0C. Grease a 20\u201322 cm springform pan.2. Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.3. Add eggs, sour cream, and salt, mix until smooth.4. Sift flour with baking powder, gently fold into the batter.5. Toss diced apples in 1 tsp cinnamon, fold half into the batter.6. Pour batter into pan, smooth the surface.7. Top with remaining apples and blueberries (toss in flour) and crumble (rub cold butter with flour and sugar).8. Bake 45\u201350 min, cover with foil after ~25 min if top browns too fast.9. Cool 10 min in pan, then transfer to a wire rack.

HIGH PROTEIN CHOCOLATE RASPBERRY CHEESECAKE \ud83c\udf53It\u2019s no surprise that I am cheesecake obsessed and this choc raspberry cheesecake is packed with over 37g of natural protein, no protein powder required!!!Of course had to add raspberry jam for a boost of fibre making it the perfect breakfast approved cheesecake. \ud83c\udf53Serves 1Ingredients:- 125g cottage cheese- 125g Greek yoghurt (I used 0% Greek yoghurt @dodoni_international ) - 10g cacao- 1 egg- 1 tbsp corn starch- 2 Tbsp maple syrup- 1/2 tsp vanilla - 60g raspberries - 1 tsp chia seedsPreheat the oven to 160 degrees Celsius. Blend the cottage cheese, Greek yoghurt, cacao, egg, maple syrup, corn starch and vanilla essence until smooth. Line an oven-safe ramekin with parchment paper to prevent sticking, then pour in the batter. Bake for about 40-50 minutes (middle should still be jiggly and sides more solid!)For the topping, add the raspberries and chia seeds to a microwave-safe dish. Couper les champignons en lamelles, les faire revenir \u00e0 la po\u00eale avec un peu d\u2019huile d\u2019olive et du sel pour retirer l\u2019eau.3. Dans un saladier, \u00e9craser le ch\u00e8vre frais. Ajouter les \u0153ufs, le lait, le sel, la muscade, les \u00e9pices et le persil. M\u00e9langer.4. Incorporer la farine et la levure.5. Cuire 40 min \u00e0 180\u00b0C.8. Servir bien chaud\u2026 et r\u00e9galez-vous \ud83d\ude0d.\ud83d\udca1 Info nutrition :Le butternut est riche en b\u00eata-carot\u00e8ne, excellent pour la peau et les d\u00e9fenses immunitaires. the best carrot cake loaf w cream cheese frosting \ud83e\udd0dHow to make:preheat to 350 degrees & baked for about 10 min (but adjust to your pan and oven) bake for 55-65 min depending on oven ingredients: dry\u20141 1/2 c AP flour, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 2 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp ground ginger, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, 1/4 tsp saltwet\u2014 2 eggs, 1/2 c olive oil, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 1/2 cups of shredded carrots, 1 cup of brown sugar, 1/3 c plain Greek yogurt ( I used @twogoodyogurt) method: mix the dry ingredients together. In a seperate bowl mix the eggs, oil & brown sugar together then add in vanilla and Greek yogurt. Then slowly stir in the wet making sure not to over mix. Fold in the shredded carrots.
